attempts.label: DANDI:000467
attempts.paper_title: Sparse and stereotyped encoding implicates a core glomerulus for ant alarm behavior
attempts.entry_title: Alarm pheromone coding in the clonal raider ant antennal lobe (Hart et al. 2023)
attempts.description: Tests the calcium imaging findings of Hart, Frank, Lopes et al. (2023) on dandiset 000467, which holds two-photon volumes of the antennal lobe of GCaMP6s ants, one file per plane and trial, for the general odorant, bilateral and alarm pheromone experiments. It maps peak responses over the whole lobe, counts responding glomeruli, identifies the focal glomeruli PGb, PGa and 6G, and measures their tuning and time course. The behaviour, transgenesis, confocal and genome data of the paper are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: The GCaMP6s line carries a single haploid transgene insertion on chromosomal scaffold 2, at Chr2 3,870,844 to 3,870,847, within an intron of trace amine-associated receptor 9; normalized read depth is about 1.5 at ObirOrco and about 0.5 over the rest of the insert.

outcomes.notes: NCBI BioProject PRJNA947257 holds one SRA experiment of whole-genome resequencing, 17 Gbases (5,561 MB), public. The Methods pipeline (Trimmomatic, bwa mem against the 220 Mb genome, Picard, samtools depth) on 17 Gbases takes hours on the runner's 4 cores, beyond the 30-minute notebook limit, and bwa, Trimmomatic and Picard are not installable from a locked pip environment. outcomes.statement: Each general odorant activates a unique combination of glomeruli, and the same odorant activates similar AL regions in different individuals.
outcomes.source: Results, Recording calcium responses to general odorants, paragraph 2; Figure 3F
outcomes.quote: each odorant activated a unique combination of glomeruli, and responses to the same odorant occurred in similar regions of the AL in different individuals
outcomes.notes: Across ants, 10 of 27 ant and odorant cases have their centroid closer to the same odorant in the other ants than to any other odorant (3-hexanone in 5 of its 6 ants; ethanol has no pixel of at least 0.2 in one ant, so 27 cases); the criterion needs more than half, and the centroid test does not depend on the M2 reading. Within ants, identical odorant pairs occur under every M2 reading (1 to 9 summed over the 6 ants; bix 7).
deviations: Stabilization by whole-pixel phase correlation in place of Fiji's Image Stabilizer; ROIs drawn by rule inside an AL mask (log-Otsu on baseline fluorescence), not by eye.

ROIs are the regions of at least 0.2 in a trial's map that recur in another trial of the odor (claims file, drawing a), a recurrence read as an overlap of at least half the smaller region, an assumption: the claims file does not say how much overlap makes a recurrence. In round 1 the pixels of at least 0.2 in two trials were taken instead, which broke the maps into fragments.
The Minimum filter uses ImageJ's radius-2 kernel (21 pixels, RankFilters); round 1 used a 13-pixel disc.
"Closer" was read as a smaller mean distance to the same odorant's centroids in the other ants than to each other odorant's centroids; the claims file does not fix the distance rule.

outcomes.statement: The breadth of responses varies across general odorants; most activate a few glomeruli, while 3-hexanone activates large regions of the ventral and medial AL.
outcomes.source: Results, Recording calcium responses to general odorants, paragraph 2; Figure 3F-G
outcomes.quote: the breadth of glomerular responses varied dramatically across odorants, with most odorants activating a few glomeruli, while 3-hexanone activated large regions of the ventral/medial AL
outcomes.notes: 3-hexanone has the largest area of at least 0.2 in its trial-averaged max projection in all 6 ants; median areas are 2,810 um2 for 3-hexanone, 1,092 for ethylpyrazine, 390 for isopropanol, 342 for propionic acid and 54 for ethanol. The ratio to ethylpyrazine is 2.57 (2.58 without the AL mask), to the others 7.2 to 51.6. In round 1, with a 13-pixel Minimum filter in place of ImageJ's 21-pixel radius-2 kernel, the ratio was 1.91 and the outcome partially reproduced; the round-1 areas are not shown by the current notebook.
deviations: Area counted inside the AL mask; the whole field of view is shown as a variant and gives the same.
The Minimum filter uses ImageJ's radius-2 kernel (21 pixels, RankFilters); round 1 used a 13-pixel disc.

outcomes.statement: Responses to 4-methyl-3-hexanol are bilaterally symmetrical in the two ALs imaged together, so later experiments imaged only the right AL.
outcomes.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 1; Figure S4A
outcomes.quote: we first imaged responses to 4-methyl-3-hexanol in both ALs simultaneously (n=3 ants) and found that response patterns were bilaterally symmetrical
outcomes.notes: Both ALs have responding ROIs in all three ants under every reading, and the mirrored maps of responding pixels correlate at r = 0.143, 0.185 and 0.072 against -0.015, -0.024 and -0.008 for the half-width shift. The ROI counts differ by more than one in at least one ant under every reading (bix 4 and 5, 4 and 8, 1 and 3; aix 5 and 8, 4 and 5, 3 and 4). One of the criterion's two parts holds in every ant, so the outcome is partial. The verifier would give not reproduced, since the criterion needs both parts and defines no partial outcome; the disagreement is recorded under verifications.
deviations: The two ALs lie one above the other in the 1X images; the midline is the least fluorescent row between 30% and 70% of the height, and the files do not say which AL is the left one.

outcomes.statement: Odors cause no fluorescence decreases; only small non-specific decreases from shifts in AL position and photobleaching occur.
outcomes.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: We did not observe any fluorescence decreases in response to odor, although we did detect small, non-specific decreases in fluorescence due to minor shifts in AL position and photobleaching
outcomes.notes: 594 regions at least 10 um across reach -0.2 or below in at least two trials of one odor at the higher concentration, in the same plane, without doing so in the vehicle trial (540 of them 10 to 20 um), in all 13 ants; the most negative has a mean of -0.452 (ant4-m4-d26-y2022, hexanol, plane 3). 168 more are negative in the vehicle trial too. Their placement points to motion, which the paper names as the source of small non-specific decreases: 487 of the 594 touch the AL border (within one 1.2 um bin) and 564 lie within 5 um of it, against 83% expected for a 10 um region placed at random in the AL; 384 overlap a negative region of another odor in the same plane (302 by half or more). The criterion counts them all, so the outcome follows the reader's rule; the vehicle comparison rests on one trial per ant.
deviations: Only each ant's higher concentration was mapped for this claim.
Stabilization by whole-pixel phase correlation, not Image Stabilizer; residual motion could produce some of the negative regions, and the vehicle comparison removes only those it shares.
A region "doing so in the vehicle trial" was read as at least half of its bins at -0.2 or below in the vehicle map of the same plane; the claims file does not say how a region is matched.

outcomes.statement: Fluorescence increases to alarm pheromones are often large (1 to 2-fold change) and outlast the 5 s odor pulse.
outcomes.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Fluorescence increases were frequently large (1–2-fold change) and lasted longer than the 5s odor presentation
outcomes.notes: No reading meets both parts. With glomerulus-sized ROIs (drawing b) the median peak fold change of responding ROI-trials is 0.453 with the mean value (445 ROI-trials, 8.8% within 1 to 2, 70.3% still above baseline mean plus 3 SD at 8.4 s) and 1.016 with the maximum (1,086, 32.7% within 1 to 2, 41.3% lasting). With drawing a the medians are 0.377 and 0.573. The criterion needs both value readings in 0.9 to 2.2 and more than half lasting.
deviations: ROIs are the regions of at least 0.2 in a trial's map that recur in another trial of the odor (claims file, drawing a), a recurrence read as an overlap of at least half the smaller region, an assumption: the claims file does not say how much overlap makes a recurrence. In round 1 the pixels of at least 0.2 in two trials were taken instead, which broke the maps into fragments.
The trace for "lasting" is the ROI's mean raw fluorescence at its depth plane, on 4 x 4 binned volumes 1 to 5 and 8, stabilized as the maps are.

The four readings b and aix keep every median at or below 6.6 (largest 3 to 6); aiy (7.8 and 8.0), aiix and aiiy (13 to 14.3) do not. Leaving out the one flagged trial changes nothing.
deviations: The paper drew ROIs by eye. The readings disagree, and the outcome rests on the ROI's mean value (ImageJ's default measure, value i) with the Methods' rule of the trial-mean value (counting x), under which both drawings (aix and bix) meet the criterion, adopted as an assumption; bix is the adopted reading throughout. All readings are shown.

outcomes.statement: Higher concentrations give more robust responses and a few more glomeruli passing the threshold, while the overall spatial pattern stays similar across concentrations.

outcomes.statement: The three compounds that elicit panic alarm (4-methyl-3-heptanone, 4-methyl-3-heptanol, 4-methyl-3-hexanol) activate partly overlapping sets of glomeruli, with a single glomerulus, PGb, activated by all three.

outcomes.notes: Only biy at 48% meets the criterion (median 1, exactly one shared ROI in 5 of 8 ants). Under bix the median number of ROIs responding to heptanone, heptanol and hexanol at one depth is 0 at the higher concentration (exactly one in 4 of 13 ants, none in 8) and 1 at 48% (exactly one in 4 of 8). aix and aiy give a median of 1 with exactly one in 5 or 6 of 13 ants; the readings ii medians of 2 to 2.5. Heptanone and hexanol share an ROI in 9 of 13 ants under bix. Leaving out the flagged trial gives the same.

outcomes.statement: 6MHO only rarely and inconsistently activates glomeruli shared with 4-methyl-3-heptanone or 4-methyl-3-hexanol.
outcomes.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 2; Figure S5C
outcomes.quote: while we sometimes observed responses to 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one and either 4-methyl-3-heptanone or 4-methyl-3-hexanol in an overlapping region, those occurrences were rare and inconsistent
outcomes.notes: The criterion asks for the result under each M2 reading, and the four readings with the ROI maximum (aiix, aiiy, biix, biiy) fail at both concentration readings, with medians 1 to 3 and shared ROIs in 11 of 13 ants at the higher concentration (met under 4 of 8 readings, under every reading False). The four readings with the ROI mean (aix, aiy, bix, biy) meet it; under bix the median number of ROIs shared by 6MHO and another pheromone is 0, with any in 1 of 13 ants (1 of 8 at 48%). With heptanone or hexanol only (the statement's wording), and without the flagged trial, the result is the same. The outcome was reproduced, resting on the ROI mean, until the third verification round agreed to the change. Under drawing a the maximum-value readings call a response from one pixel of at least 0.2 in mostly sub-glomerular regions (ant1-m4-d27 has 27 shared ROIs under biix and none under bix), so the failure may come from that reading as much as from the data.
deviations: ROIs are the regions of at least 0.2 in a trial's map that recur in another trial of the odor (claims file, drawing a), a recurrence read as an overlap of at least half the smaller region, an assumption: the claims file does not say how much overlap makes a recurrence. In round 1 the pixels of at least 0.2 in two trials were taken instead, which broke the maps into fragments.

outcomes.statement: The three pheromones with overlapping AL responses all elicit panic alarm, while 6MHO does not elicit panic and gives a non-overlapping response, pointing to a shared pathway for panic alarm centred on PGb.

outcomes.quote: The three pheromones with overlapping calcium response patterns all robustly elicited panic alarm behavior, while 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one did not elicit panic alarm behavior and generated a non-overlapping response
outcomes.notes: Imaging half only. figs5b-shared-glomerulus is not met under any reading at the higher concentration and only under biy at 48%; figs5c-mho-rarely-overlaps is met under the four mean-value readings and fails under the four maximum-value readings, so it is not reproduced. The behaviour half rests on fig1e-categorical-response, whose data are not in the dataset.
deviations: Judged on figs5b-shared-glomerulus and figs5c-mho-rarely-overlaps as tested here.

outcomes.statement: PGb lies in the anterior ventral hemi-lobe next to a gap without glomeruli, about halfway between the dorsal and ventral AL surfaces, with two neighbouring alarm-responsive glomeruli in the same plane; PGb and 6G were found in 13 of 13 ants and PGa in 11 of 13.
outcomes.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 1; Figure 5A-B
outcomes.quote: PG b is located approximately halfway between the dorsal and ventral AL surfaces, and is neighbored by two additional glomeruli that respond to alarm pheromones, with all three visible in the same optical plane ... Both glomeruli were identified in 13/13 individuals. In 11/13 individuals, we identified a third neighboring glomerulus
outcomes.notes: No M2 reading gives all three counts within tolerance; PGb is identified in 5 to 12 of 13 ants, 6G in 1 to 10 and PGa in 0 to 4 (bix 5, 2, 0, given as measured; aiix 12, 10, 3; aiiy 12, 10, 4). With the deepest AL plane where the AL's baseline fluorescence falls to 25% of its brightest plane, PGb lies in the middle third of the depth in 1 to 3 ants per reading (bix 1 of 5; the other 4 at 0.71 to 0.77 of the depth). With a 10% rule 5 to 11 ants per reading are in the middle third.
deviations: The identification follows M4 with "adjacent" read as centres at most 20 um apart (two touching glomeruli of at most 20 um, Results); the claims file does not give a distance.
The deepest plane with AL fluorescence was read with a 25% rule, with 10% and 50% shown; the claims file does not give one.

ROIs are the regions of at least 0.2 in a trial's map that recur in another trial of the odor (claims file, drawing a), a recurrence read as an overlap of at least half the smaller region, an assumption: the claims file does not say how much overlap makes a recurrence. In round 1 the pixels of at least 0.2 in two trials were taken instead, which broke the maps into fragments.

outcomes.statement: PGa is always anterior (12.9 +/- 1.9 SD um) and slightly lateral (5.1 +/- 2.9 um) to PGb, and 6G always lateral to PGb (13.1 +/- 2.6 um) at a similar anterior-posterior position (0.6 +/- 2.2 um); the SDs are much smaller than a glomerulus diameter, so the three occupy stereotyped positions.
outcomes.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 3; Figure 5D
outcomes.quote: PG a was always located anterior (mean distance between centers: 12.9±1.9SD μm), and slightly lateral (mean distance: 5.1±2.9SD μm) to PG b ( Fig. 5D ). In comparison, 6G was always lateral to PG b (mean distance: 13.1±2.6SD μm), and in a similar position along the anterior-posterior axis (mean distance: 0.6±2.2SD μm)
outcomes.notes: No reading meets the criterion, so the readings do not disagree on the outcome. Under bix no PGa is identified, and 6G (2 ants) lies 12.9 to 15.6 um lateral and 0.1 to 3.5 um anterior of PGb on average under the centre readings ac, ad, bc and bd. Under the other readings PGa (2 to 4 ants) lies 9.2 to 18.5 um anterior on average (expected 12.9 +/- 1.9) with SDs up to 13.1 um, and 0.4 to 9.8 um lateral with SDs up to 14.0 um; 6G (1 to 10 ants) lies 7.6 to 20.8 um lateral with SDs of 1.3 to 8.8 um. The image axes are those the files give ("up is lateral, right is anterior"); a baseline image of ant1-m4-d26-y2022 with the three centres marked shows PGa anterior and 6G lateral of PGb, as in Figure 5B. The direction conditions do not hold in every ant under every reading, since the centres are taken again after identification; PGa is not anterior in every ant under aiiy bc, biix bd and biiy bd, and 6G is not lateral in every ant under aiix bd, aiiy ad and bd, aiy ad and bd, biix ac and biiy ac.
deviations: Centres were taken on 4 x 4 binned per-plane maps (1.16 um) in PGb's plane.

M4 identifies PGa and 6G by their direction from PGb, but the centres measured here are taken again on the defining odors' maps, so the direction conditions are tested and do not hold by construction (round 1 said they did, which the outputs do not show).

outcomes.statement: PGb, PGa and 6G each respond to a unique combination of pheromones, with several pheromone and glomerulus pairs giving no response; PGb responds to 4-methyl-3-heptanone, 4-methyl-3-heptanol and 4-methyl-3-hexanol and not to 6MHO, PGa to 4-methyl-3-heptanol and 4-methyl-3-hexanol, and 6G to 6MHO.
outcomes.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 2; Figure 5C; Figure S6
outcomes.quote: while PG b , PG a , and 6G are spatially adjacent, they each reliably respond to unique combinations of odorants, with several pheromone/glomerulus combinations producing no detectable responses ... PG b did not respond to 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one
outcomes.notes: With the disc, PGb responds at 48% to heptanone, heptanol and hexanol under both identifications, both plane readings and both models (plane a, model a: bix 0.851, 0.678, 0.734 with 5 ants; aiiy 0.596, 0.327, 0.528 with 12 ants), all with CIs above 0, and 6G responds to 6MHO (0.335 with 2 ants, 0.280 with 10). PGa is not identified under bix; under aiiy (4 ants) it responds to heptanol (0.258 to 0.274) and its hexanol prediction is 0.164 to 0.191 with the CI above 0, short of 0.2, so 5 of the 6 named combinations respond. PGb's prediction for 6MHO is negative with its CI below 0 (-0.087, -0.084), which the criterion counts as neither a response nor no response. The sets of PGb, PGa and 6G differ under the disc. With the region ROI, which takes in neighbours within 17.5 um, PGb responds to 6MHO in some fits and under aiiy the sets differ in one of four fits. No reading meets the whole criterion; the PGb and 6G parts hold. For the region ROI, 618 of the 1,684 traces had no disc pixel of at least 0.2 and fell back to the disc, which narrows the difference between the two ROIs.
deviations: The single-glomerulus traces are computed for two identifications, bix (the adopted M2 reading) and aiiy (the reading that identifies PGa in the most ants, chosen in the notebook by that rule), for both plane readings and both of the claims file's ROIs (the 15 um disc and the region of at least 0.2 at the centre). aiiy uses the ROI's maximum and drawing a, the reading set aside for the counts of figs5a-sparse-median-6, and 356 of drawing a's 436 regions are under 10 um across; it is used only because it finds PGa in the most ants, and the PGa results rest on it.

The outcome rests on the disc ROI (the claims file's first M3 ROI and the typical glomerulus of Figure 5D), adopted as an assumption: the region of at least 0.2 is chosen on the same trial's peak map and absorbs neighbouring glomeruli.

Each plane's row band is stabilized (phase correlation against the baseline mean, as for the maps); the unstabilized disc trace is kept for comparison (PGb peak fold change, median absolute difference 0.035, largest 0.591, r = 0.98; 3 of 129 trials change side of 0.2). Volume times include the centre plane's offset in the volume scan (0.0335 s per plane, from the files' starting_time).
The model of reading (a) predicts for the average ant (sum-coded ant effects).

outcomes.statement: Responses in PGb and PGa peak and then decline close to baseline by the end of the 48 s recording, while 6G responses to 6MHO are very slow, with a plateau of tens of seconds.

With the region ROI the PGb heptanol trace ends at 0.272 to 0.472 and the criterion fails. For the region ROI, 618 of the 1,684 traces fell back to the disc (no disc pixel of at least 0.2).

outcomes.statement: In 144 s recordings, 6G responses to 6MHO plateau for about 30 s and return to baseline about 80 s after odor presentation, sometimes taking more than 100 s.
outcomes.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 2; Figure S7A
outcomes.quote: Fluorescence plateaued for ~30s before declining and returning to baseline ~80s after odor presentation
outcomes.notes: Under aiiy 6G is identified in all 5 ants with a 144 s recording (under bix in 1). With the region ROI the return is 70.8 to 91.5 s but the plateau 7.2 to 15.7 s. Under the disc one trial returns more than 100 s after odor presentation (100.7 to 105.7 s by onset reading); under the region ROI with return reading b two trials do (105.9 to 110.9 s and 100.7 to 105.7 s). outcomes.statement: Onset and peak times differ by pheromone and glomerulus; for PGb and PGa responses to 4-methyl-3-heptanol and 4-methyl-3-hexanol, onset time depends on pheromone, glomerulus and their interaction, and time to maximum on pheromone and glomerulus but not their interaction.
outcomes.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 2; Figure S7C legend
outcomes.quote: Time to response onset: significant effects of pheromone (p=0.0034), glomerulus (p<0.0001), and the interaction (p=0.0030). Time to response maximum: significant effects of pheromone (p<0.0001) and glomerulus (p=0.047), but not the interaction (p=0.88)

outcomes.notes: Under bix no PGa is identified, so the models cannot be fitted (one glomerulus level; the notebook lists each as NOT TESTED). Under aiiy, which identifies PGa in 4 of 13 ants (3 at 48%), the models fit with 18 PGa and 48 PGb traces at 48% (with the disc 8 or 9 PGa traces never exceed the bound and are excluded, with the region 2 or 3; 1 PGb trace with the disc). Across the 12 combinations of ROI, plane and p-value reading, 1 to 4 of the 5 effects have p < 0.05, and the time-to-maximum interaction has p < 0.05 in 9 of 12, where the paper reports p = 0.88. Of the 24 sets of fits, 23 converged; the ML fits of reading (a) for onset with the region ROI and plane a did not. The evidence is weak, with PGa from 3 ants against the paper's 8.
deviations: The single-glomerulus traces are computed for two identifications, bix (the adopted M2 reading) and aiiy (the reading that identifies PGa in the most ants, chosen in the notebook by that rule), for both plane readings and both of the claims file's ROIs (the 15 um disc and the region of at least 0.2 at the centre). aiiy uses the ROI's maximum and drawing a, the reading set aside for the counts of figs5a-sparse-median-6, and 356 of drawing a's 436 regions are under 10 um across; it is used only because it finds PGa in the most ants, and the PGa results rest on it.
The outcome rests on the aiiy identification, the only one under which the claim can be tested; under the adopted bix it cannot.

Each plane's row band is stabilized (phase correlation against the baseline mean, as for the maps); the unstabilized disc trace is kept for comparison (PGb peak fold change, median absolute difference 0.035, largest 0.591, r = 0.98; 3 of 129 trials change side of 0.2). findings.statement: The planes' starting_time values step by 0.0335 s, so a 33-plane volume takes 1.105 s, while each file's imaging_rate is 0.83 volumes/s (1.205 s per volume) and the paper states 27.5 frames/s and a volume every 1.2 s. The data do not show which is right; the analysis times volumes by the imaging rate.

The odor, concentration and trial are given only in the file and session names and the stimulus timing (onset 3 s, 5 s pulse) only in free-text descriptions; the files hold no stimulus or trial table. The bilateral files do not say which antennal lobe is the left one.

Each file holds one plane of one trial as uncompressed float64, although the values are 13-bit integers (0 to 8191), so the dandiset is 14,685 files and 1.26 TB. A whole-lobe analysis of the alarm experiment must open about 11,600 files; this attempt read about half a terabyte through range requests.
The general odorant files hold the five odorants the paper analyses and the vehicle; the paper says 7 to 9 odorants were presented, and the dandiset does not say that the others were left out.

Questions for the paper's authors. How were the ROIs drawn on the max projections (any size or shape rule, how adjacent glomeruli were separated), was an ROI's value its mean or its maximum, and was "responding" judged on the trial-mean value (Methods) or per trial and averaged (Figure S5 legend)? This attempt adopted the ROI's mean and the trial-mean rule, with glomerulus-sized ROIs for the focal glomeruli; the counts of responding glomeruli, the vehicle responses and the identification of PGb, 6G and PGa depend on these choices.

Questions for the paper's authors. Which trials were excluded for motion artifacts, and by what rule? How was the centre plane of a glomerulus chosen, and what ROI was measured on the three-plane projection? What distance makes two glomeruli adjacent when identifying 6G and PGa?
No file or trial is deposited twice. All 14,685 assets have distinct content, and no two trials of an ant have identical baseline volumes in the maps computed.

disagreements.reason: 3-hexanone has the largest area in 6 of 6 ants, but its median area over ethylpyrazine's is 1.91, short of the required 2. The ratio is 1.91 with and without the AL mask. A near miss.
Under every ROI reading at least one ant's two ALs differ by more than one ROI (e.g. bix: 4 vs 7). The correlation part holds.
No reading meets both parts. b/i median 0.59, 75% still elevated after the pulse. b/ii median 1.18, but only 46% elevated. Under the unfiltered readings the medians are 0.37 and 0.42.

Under all four size-filtered readings, at 48% and at each ant's higher concentration, the largest median is 3 to 4 (limit 6.6). Under all four unfiltered readings it is 33 to 48. Those counts come from noise fragments (problem 4).
Both parts hold only under bix and biy. The sign test fails under biix and biiy (p 0.48 and 0.13). The lower-set-within-higher-set part fails under every unfiltered reading (8 to 17 of 52 pairs).
No reading meets it. Best is bix: median 1, but exactly one shared ROI in only 6 of 13 ants (needs more than 6.5) and 4 of 8 at 48% (needs more than 4).
Met only under bix and biy. Fails under the other six readings (medians 1 to 4.5).

disagreements.reason: I still think this is not_reproduced. The criterion needs both parts in every ant, defines no partial outcome, and the count part fails under every reading (cell 14). This is a classification point and the disagreement is recorded.

The criterion says "Reproduced when, under each M2 reading...". The four ROI-maximum readings fail: medians 1 to 3, with shared ROIs in 11 of 13 ants (cell 21). entries.name: 000467-hart-2023
entries.title: Alarm pheromone coding in the clonal raider ant antennal lobe (Hart et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the calcium imaging findings of Hart, Frank, Lopes et al. (2023) on dandiset 000467, which holds two-photon volumes of the antennal lobe of GCaMP6s ants, one file per plane and trial, for the general odorant, bilateral and alarm pheromone experiments. It maps peak responses over the whole lobe, counts responding glomeruli, identifies the focal glomeruli PGb, PGa and 6G, and measures their tuning and time course. The behaviour, transgenesis, confocal and genome data of the paper are not in the dandiset.
